revised.summary:
The operator gets a Screens list and screen commands that never reach a show app by accident. Today 'screen identify all' can flash PlayMap's outputs, and 'screen disconnect all' drops every peer's link. After this change:
- A show app that proves itself is listed under Producer → Show network, not Screens. It proves itself with a node key, or with the operator's own control key or PIN.
- Each Show network row has a link line and a shape mark (✓ node key, △ operator credential, ○ unverified). Its right-click menu offers Copy node id, Let a key speak for this node, and Revoke its key.
- An app that only claims to be a show app stays in Screens, flagged 'claims to be patterns 9f8e… (unproven)'. 'all' never reaches it, but the operator can still target it by its id, so a stray client can always be dropped.
- A screen command that names a proven app is refused with the reason. A peer can never use its own name to shadow a browser's name.
- PlayMap turns an 'identify' from any Stagewatch into a journal row, never OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL. This ships first and needs nothing else.

Keys get stronger, without anyone losing the timer:
- One node key speaks for exactly one node id, and an id with a key is spoken for only with that key. This holds on every route that writes for a node: the context, proposals, collect and result.
- The check runs before anything is stored. A forged context can no longer relabel the risk on another app's proposals, and an open (unverified) context never lowers a risk.
- A key shared between two installs keeps both of them following the countdown. Only the second install's context and approvals are refused, with words that name both ids.
- The binding is saved with the key. The operator moves it explicitly ('Let it speak for…', with buttons and a right-click menu in step), so there is no first-come race.
- Revoking a key, or changing the PIN, now reaches open sockets at once: a key-authenticated socket falls back to the public frame, and a PIN-authenticated control page loses control. The only close is the one the viewing code already does.
- Unknown or revoked keys stop counting toward the 5-a-minute address lockout. A 160-bit key cannot be guessed. Today, a peer holding a revoked key locks its whole machine out of the PIN through its ordinary polling.

Each app gets its own identity on /ws: ?node=<its Show Bus id>&t=<kind>, plus cid=<id> so an older Stagewatch also lists the installs apart. A node link hears Stagewatch's verdict before any frame. Each app records a refusal before doing anything else and holds its keyed calls for 60 s:
- Patterns shows the refusal on the Eye, the Nodes page, the context and the assistant (all through ShowApps), in STATE bus.stagewatch.key, and in the Companion variable stagewatch_key. It also says when its id cannot be kept.
- AGMessage says 'connected' and confirms its TLS pin only on the verdict or an authenticated 2xx. Participants see only the coarse status; admins see the words.
- PlayMap's 'paired' becomes honest (Paired or NotNeeded). Preflight shows a refused key as its own state, not 'not heard'.

The screen verb's rules move out of the WPF view model, so the suite, the rig and the desk run one code path. The full design is at /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/peers-not-screens.md; §9 answers each review item.

decisions.decision: A node link names itself on /ws with ?node=<Show Bus id>&t=<hello kind>. The credential goes in Authorization: Bearer. Peers also send cid=<id>&page=/<app>, which a new Stagewatch ignores when node is present.
decisions.why: The hello id is the identity on every other Show Bus surface (Stagewatch/docs/SHOWBUS.md:39,194). It is per install and not a secret (§1 rule 5). cid=<id> means an older Stagewatch also lists each install under its own id, so G32 is fixed even there. The fixed cids today are Patterns StagewatchLinkService.cs:276 and AGMessage nodes.js:317. AGMessage's id is 8 hex (server.js:82).
decisions.alternatives:
- The id as cid only: keeps the apps in Screens.
- A first hello message: races the first frame.

decisions.decision:
Which sockets are nodes:
- A socket with a valid node-scope key is a node link, with or without node=.
- A node= link with the operator's credential (a control key or the PIN) is a node link too.
- A node= with no credential, a read or MCP key, or a refused key is a claim. A claim stays in Screens, flagged, is skipped by 'all' and by no target, and is reachable by its own screen id or by an operator-given name.
decisions.why: Anything on the LAN can put node= in a URL (review item 3). Disconnect is 'for a stray tablet' (WebServer.cs:100-103), so the operator must keep a handle on unproven sockets. Keeping claims out of 'all' still closes G06 for keyless PlayMaps. The node scope exists only for show apps (ApiKeys.cs:16-20).
decisions.alternatives:
- Claims included in 'all': G06's harm returns for keyless peers.
- Claims taken out of Screens: no handle on a stray client.

decisions.decision:
One node, one key on every route that writes for a node (NodeBindings.Speak in Core):
- A node key speaks only for its bound id. It binds on its first proven use (a node link, a context, a proposal's from, or a collect).
- A key-bound id is refused to the PIN, a control key or an open request.
- The check runs before anything is stored, queued or claimed.
- A context of weaker proof never replaces a stronger one for the same id within KeepFor.
decisions.why: G15 worked because the check came after the store and its false was ignored (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:64-70; ShowBus.cs:58-70), and because non-node credentials were never checked (Approvals.cs:92,137,149-154). A control key passes the Node gate (ApiKeys.cs:76-77).
decisions.alternatives:
- G15's minimal fix (refuse only node keys): leaves forgery with the PIN, a control key or an open request.
- Tie an id to an address: DHCP and two-NIC laptops move, and no cause has been measured.

decisions.decision: On /ws a binding conflict never stops the frames. The node link is listed verified:'none', with words such as 'this key speaks for patterns 9f8e7d6c'. Only the node routes answer 403. A legacy keyed socket (no node=) is listed under its key ('names no node id'), never under the binding's id.
decisions.why: The shared-key case (review item 2): a Patterns twin, or two AGMessages given one key, must keep the countdown, which is their core function. The binding governs contexts and approvals, not reading. Today /ws ignores the binding (WebServer.cs:1141-1219).
decisions.alternatives: Refuse and close: the second holder loses the timer over a rule about approvals.

decisions.decision: Unknown or revoked keys never count toward the address lockout. Wrong PINs, wrong viewing codes and wrong window addresses still do.
decisions.why: A key is 160 bits (ApiKeys.cs:50-55) and cannot be guessed, so counting it protects nothing. It does let a peer with a revoked key lock its whole machine out of the PIN. Today the peers' polling already does this: Patterns posts every 5 s and polls the queue every 2 s (StagewatchLinkService.cs:347-353), PlayMap does the same (StagewatchLink.cs:469-472), and AGMessage pushes every ≤5 s (server.js:1114-1125). A redial loop would do it faster. Removing the cost beats governing it.
decisions.alternatives: Keep counting and rely on each peer honouring 'retry': fails for every peer already deployed, because all three reset their backoff on an upgrade (nodes.js:322-324; StagewatchLinkService.cs:182-186; StagewatchLink.cs:236-250).

decisions.decision: No new close for a key reason; only the viewing code still closes. A socket whose key is refused at admission, or revoked later, hears one {type:'auth',ok:false,error,retry:60} and stays open as a public viewer. With a viewing code set, that same single message carries view:true and the socket closes, as today.
decisions.why: Old peers turn any close into a 0.5 s loop (review item 1). The precedent: a control socket with a wrong PIN already hears ok:false and stays open as a viewer (WebServer.cs:1163-1164,1191,1213-1219). Pages ignore an auth message without view (common.js:106,109).
decisions.alternatives: A 401 or 403 at upgrade with Retry-After. Correcting the first version: it IS readable, through .NET 7+ CollectHttpResponseDetails and ws 'unexpected-response'. But it would stop the timer for a key problem on an open Stagewatch, and without the lockout change it is not lockout-safe either, because old peers' backoff still reaches 5 s.

decisions.decision: The verdict is in-band and first, on node links only: {type:'auth',ok:true,scope,node:{t,id,verified},words?} or the refusal line. It is sent again on revoke, rebind or a PIN change (latest wins). Legacy sockets with an accepted key hear nothing new. Malformed node requests get an HTTP 400 before the upgrade: key in the URL, Window scheme, win, role=control, bad id or kind, own id.
decisions.why: Attempts are not facts: the peer learns at the socket what Stagewatch made of its claim. spec-1-3's leases (§12.4) and windows-for-peers' grants need a 'key-verified node link'. Third-party clients still see a frame first (ShowBusTests.cs:210-220). Each verdict is also reachable over HTTP through the context POST's verified field, so peers fall back to HTTP against an older Stagewatch.
decisions.alternatives:
- No in-band verdict, HTTP only: sibling designs lose their key-verified link fact.
- A verdict on every socket: breaks clients that read the first frame.

decisions.decision:
CredentialsChanged() re-checks open sockets whenever keys or the PIN change (it is called from RefreshScreenCopies):
- A key gone: the socket downgrades to the public frame, and a node link becomes a claim.
- A PIN changed: a PIN-admitted control socket loses control and hears 'the PIN changed'.
- A rebind: verified is recomputed.
Nothing ever closes on a NodeOf mismatch.
decisions.why: Revoking only rewrote the list (MainViewModel.Screens.cs:84-91), while ReadKey and CanControl were fixed at admission (WebServer.cs:1191,1417,1425). 'Revoking works at once' (SettingsDialog.xaml:304) was untrue for live sockets. RefreshScreenCopies runs on every key change and after Settings closes (MainViewModel.cs:919-922). Review item 6: a legacy socket that binds its own key by its own context POST must stay open.
decisions.alternatives: Re-check credentials on every frame: costs on the send loop, with no gain.

decisions.decision: The binding is persisted on the key (ApiKey.node, nodeKind). The operator rebinds explicitly: 'Let this key speak for <node>…' in Settings (a button plus right-click, in step) and on the Show network row's right-click. The dialog offers the id that key was just refused for.
decisions.why: The in-memory binding reopens a race at every restart (Approvals.cs:50,63-74), and a reinstalled peer has a new id. Writing an explicit pair has no race. 'Release, then first come' lost to the old holder's fast redial (review item 5).
decisions.alternatives: Release with retry 1: a race that the intended new holder loses.

decisions.decision: An unverified context (Proof None) is kept and labelled, and its commands never set a proposal's risk (unknown = high). Patterns' context, pulled over Stagewatch's own proof-paired link, counts as Key.
decisions.why: This closes the LAN-forgery half of G15 without breaking an open show's Show network. RiskFor reads the entry today (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:73-84).
decisions.alternatives: Refuse every unauthenticated context: breaks open shows for no gain over gating the risk.

decisions.decision:
The screen verb's rules move to Timer.Remote/ScreenDirector.cs, with a fixed matching order:
1. 'all' or empty: browsers only, never control pages or claims.
2. A screen id (claims included).
3. An operator-given screen name.
4. Only then, a proven node's id or a key-verified node's name: refused 'is a show app'.
5. Otherwise, nothing matches.
No node-disconnect verb is added.
decisions.why: Screens.Match falls back to names (Screens.cs:61-68), and a peer chooses its own name (review item 12). The suite cannot load Timer.App (Stagewatch.Tests.csproj:16-25), and the rig refuses screen (Rig Program.cs:182-201). Revoking the key is the real wall.
decisions.alternatives: Refuse by any node name: a peer named 'Lobby TV' could block the operator's TV.

decisions.decision: Peers record a refusal in a field before any I/O and honour it on every exit path. On a 401 or ok:false, keyed calls (and a closed link's redial) wait 'retry' seconds (60, or Retry-After for a 429). A 403 binding refusal holds nothing. A new key typed into the peer restarts its link, so no 'dial again now' control is needed.
decisions.why: PlayMap's hold came only from a normal return, and the CloseOutputAsync race threw it away (StagewatchLink.cs:243-250,362-365). Patterns has the same shape (StagewatchLinkService.cs:182-200). A 403 does not count toward the lockout and is answered within 5 s once the operator rebinds.
decisions.alternatives: A hold only from Take's return value: lost to the close race.

decisions.decision:
PlayMap:
- identify is always a journal row.
- paired = Pairing is Paired or NotNeeded.
- A refused key is STATE links.stagewatch.state 'refused', with its own preflight arm (no fix line, because the fix is on Stagewatch).
- ContextBuilder.cs and Seams.cs, both spine files, are not edited.
decisions.why: OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL 5 ran through a Remote session (NetworkHost.cs:776-784). Counting only Paired would turn keyless links amber, whereas the Patterns link counts NotNeeded (PatternsLink.cs:142). Preflight's red 'not heard' with LINK STAGEWATCH is the wrong remedy (PreflightBreadth.cs:117-129). The context item already reads state and detail (ContextBuilder.cs:96-100).
decisions.alternatives:
- Flash the name on the timer surface: it may be on air.
- paired = Paired only: a regression.

decisions.decision: The bindings fail closed by default. IShowAccess.Nodes => NodeBindings.For(this), a per-implementer ConditionalWeakTable instance that enforces first-bind-wins. The checks visible in a request (context node.id, proposal from.id, collect target) run in WebServer before the implementation is called; result is checked in ProposalDesk.
decisions.why: A null default would run the node routes unchecked (review item 15). Six fakes implement IShowControl through defaults (ShowState.cs:497-507).
decisions.alternatives: A required member: forces six fakes to change for no extra safety.

decisions.decision: The rig makes its own keys (--node-keys N, through ApiKeys.Create). It saves their hashes and bindings in its --state file and reports the secrets made in that run in its ready line, as it already reports the PIN. No Core API builds a key from a chosen secret.
decisions.why: ApiKeys.Create is the only maker (ApiKeys.cs:48-65), and the rig already prints its PIN (Rig Program.cs:12,132-137).
decisions.alternatives: ApiKeys.FromSecret: a shipping API that bypasses 'random secret, shown once'.

revised.wire:
STAGEWATCH (Show Bus 1.3 words for §6 peers fields, §7 one node one key, §7.1 node links and §11 bound ids, carried by spec-1-3's single master edit)

1) WebSocket node link
GET /ws?node=<id>&t=<kind>[&detail=1][&cid=<id>&page=/<app>]
Authorization: Bearer <node key | control key | PIN>, or no header (a claim)
- id = [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}; kind = [a-z0-9_-]{1,16}.
- With node, cid and page are ignored.

Refused before the upgrade: HTTP 400 {"ok":false,"error":…}, never counted toward the lockout.
- node with win, or Authorization: Window … → "a window's link is not a node link"
- node with ?pin= → "a node link carries its key in the Authorization header, never in the URL"
- node with role=control → "a node link reads; it does not control"
- a bad id → "a node id is 1-40 letters, digits, - or _"
- a bad or missing t → "a node link names its kind (t=patterns, playmap, messenger…)"
- this Stagewatch's own id → "that's this Stagewatch"

Admission order:
1. The credential (Authorize or CheckPin as today; an unknown key is no longer counted).
2. The viewing code (one message).
3. The class:
   - node key K bound to this id, or unbound and the id free (binds now) → node, verified key
   - K bound elsewhere, or the id bound to another key → node, verified none + words (frames continue)
   - control key or PIN, id not key-bound → node, verified operator
   - control key or PIN, id key-bound → node, verified none + words
   - read or MCP key, or none → claim (in Screens, flagged, never in 'all')
   - refused key → claim + the ok:false line

First message on a node link, before any frame:
- {"type":"auth","ok":true,"scope":"node|control|read|mcp|pin|none","node":{"t":"patterns","id":"9f8e7d6c","verified":"key|operator|none"}}
- "words" is appended only when verified is none. It is one of:
  - "no key — the id is only claimed"
  - "a read key reads; only a node key speaks for a node"
  - "this key speaks for <kind> <id> — the Stagewatch operator can let it speak for this one"
  - "<kind> <id> speaks with its own key"
- A refused key: {"type":"auth","ok":false,"error":"unknown or revoked API key"|"too many wrong PINs — wait a minute"|"wrong PIN"|"rate limit: too many requests with this key","retry":60|Retry-After}
  - The socket stays open with the public frame.
  - With a viewing code set, the same single message carries "view":true and the socket closes, as today.

Legacy sockets (no node=):
- Admission is unchanged.
- A refused key (header or ?pin=swk_) on a non-control socket hears the one ok:false line and stays open.
- An accepted key hears nothing new.
- A valid node-scope key makes the socket a node link listed by its key, with no id asserted.
- Control sockets keep their existing auth messages.

While linked (latest wins):
- Key revoked → {"type":"auth","ok":false,"error":"this key was revoked","retry":60}, then the public frame (a close only under a viewing code). This applies to node links and legacy keyed sockets alike.
- Key rebound → a fresh ok:true verdict.
- PIN changed → a PIN-admitted control socket hears {"type":"auth","ok":false,"error":"the PIN changed — enter the new one"} and stays a viewer.
- A node link never receives redirect, identify, reload or disconnect. A claim receives them only when targeted explicitly.

2) HTTP: one node, one key
Credential per request (CredentialOf):
- node key → Key(keyId)
- control key, or the PIN when one is set and given → Operator
- anything else → None

Routes:
- POST /api/peers/context (body node.id), POST /api/proposals (from.id; was 400, now 403), GET /api/proposals?target=<id>&state=approved
  - Checked in WebServer before the implementation.
  - 403 {"ok":false,"error":"this key speaks for <kind> <id>"}
  - 403 {"ok":false,"error":"<kind> <id> speaks with its own key"}
  - contexts only: 403 {"ok":false,"error":"<kind> <id> spoke with a stronger proof 12 s ago"}
- POST /api/proposals/<id>/result → 409 as today, with the same words (checked in ProposalDesk).
- A context is accepted with 200 {"ok":true,"verified":"key|operator|none"} (field appended).
- Binding refusals never count toward the lockout.
- An unknown or revoked key still gets 401, and is no longer counted.
- A Proof-None context is kept, labelled unverified, and never sets a proposal's risk.

3) Context §6 peers rows
{"t","id","name","light","headline","heard","link":"ws"|"","verified":"key"|"operator"|"none"|""}
- The last two fields are appended.
- link is "ws" only for a proven node link (verified key or operator).
- A link-only row is listed only for a proven id. Claims, conflicts and legacy keyed sockets never add a row.
- Rows are capped at 32 (PeerContexts.MaxPeers). MCP get_context returns the same.

4) Screens
- GET /api/screens rows gain "claim":"patterns 9f8e7d6c"|"" at the end.
- screen identify|reload|disconnect|go|save|name match in this order: 'all' or empty (browsers only, no claims); a screen id; an operator-given name; then a proven node's id or a key-verified node's name, refused.
- Refusal: "Screens: 9f8e7d6c is a show app (Patterns FOH), not a screen — screen commands reach browsers only (Producer → Show network)". It appears in the HTTP, WS, OSC, Companion TCP and MCP receipts.

5) Settings JSON
remote.apiKeys[] gains "node":"<id>" and "nodeKind":"<t>", appended, kept only on node-scope keys with a valid id and kind.

6) No new verb, no new hello cap, no new frame field.

PATTERNS
- Dials ws(s)://<sw>/ws?node=<ShowBusId>&t=patterns&cid=<ShowBusId>&page=/patterns with Authorization: Bearer.
- STATE bus.stagewatch gains "key" last (after "stuck" if that round lands first): "key|operator|none|refused|"""
  - from the verdict, else from the context POST's verified, else "refused" on a 401;
  - "" means Stagewatch said neither.
- Companion variable stagewatch_key.

AGMESSAGE
- Dials /ws?node=<nodeId>&t=messenger&cid=<nodeId>&page=%2Fagmessage with Authorization: Bearer.
- With a key, 'connecting' until auth ok:true with a scope other than none, or an authenticated GET /api/context 2xx (judged by status). The TLS pin is confirmed only then.
- With no key, the first state frame (unchanged).
- A refusal gives the sticky status 'key refused' and holds keyed calls for 'retry' s.
- socket.io:
  - the shared 'stage' event carries status from a closed set (connected, connecting, reconnecting, stale, key refused, certificate refused, off);
  - a new admin-only 'stageLink' {status, words, until} carries the refusal's words.

PLAYMAP
- Dials /ws?node=<NodeId>&t=playmap&cid=<cid>&page=/playmap&detail=1 with Authorization: Bearer.
- STATE links.stagewatch:
  - paired = Pairing is Paired or NotNeeded;
  - state "refused" when the key is refused and the link is not live (a new value);
  - detail "key refused — <Stagewatch's words>".
- An identify from any Stagewatch gives a journal row, never OUTPUT IDENTIFY ALL.

changes.change:
Adds NodeProof {None, Operator, Key}, record struct NodeCredential(KeyId, Proof) and record struct NodeVerdict(Ok, Proof, Error).

NodeBindings holds key ↔ (kind, id) under a lock, seeded from ApiKey.Node/NodeKind. It raises Bound(keyId, kind, id, previousId?) outside the lock.

Methods:
- Speak(cred, kind, id): binds on first proven use, refuses both ways, and refuses non-key credentials for a key-bound id.
- Rebind(keyId, kind, id): the operator's choice; moves the id off any other key.
- LastRefused(keyId), NodeOf, KeyOf, Keep(liveKeyIds), ValidId, ValidKind.
- static For(owner): a ConditionalWeakTable instance, the fail-closed default.

Adds the records WsCredential, WsAdmission (class: screen, claim or node; verified; words; the 400 error; the first message's bytes) and NodeLinkFact(Kind, Id, Verified, KeyId, KeyName, Address, ConnectedUtc, Links, Words).

Two pure functions:
- NodeLinks.Admit(query, authScheme, cred, viewNeeded, ownId, bindings): the whole §2.1 matrix, including the pre-upgrade 400s.
- NodeLinks.Recheck(socketState, keys, bindings, pinHash): the new state and the message to send when a credential changes. It never closes except under a viewing code.

risks: A shared key loses its approvals, never its timer. An operator who pasted one node key into several installs sees the second install's context and proposals refused (403 'this key speaks for patterns 9f8e7d6c'), where today its context is stored. Mitigations: the words, a journal row naming the key and both ids, a release note ('one node key per install') and 'Let it speak for…'.

Persisted bindings: a peer reinstalled with a new id is refused on the node routes until the operator rebinds its key. Mitigation: the rebind dialog offers the id that key was just refused for, and the journal row names both ids.

The lockout rule changes: unknown or revoked keys no longer count. A 160-bit key cannot be guessed, and wrong PINs, viewing codes and window addresses still count. REMOTE.md:214 is corrected in the same unit. A valid key from an address locked by wrong PINs is still refused, as today.

CredentialsChanged runs on the show thread over the ConcurrentDictionary of sockets. It only sets volatile flags and sends through Task.Run, like Push, and never waits.

An older peer against the new Stagewatch gets no new close and no lockout from its revoked key. issues.issue: Rollout hazard: Stagewatch ships first (every peer unit depends on SW-3), but the peers already deployed redial fast. The design now closes sockets that carry a refused header key and sockets whose key is revoked, including legacy sockets with no node=. Old peers reset their backoff whenever the upgrade succeeds: AGMessage sets delay=500 in onopen, and Patterns and PlayMap set attempt=0 when the connection returns normally. So upgrade, verdict, close and redial repeat about every 0.5 s. Each dial with an unknown or revoked key counts toward the 5-a-minute lockout, so within seconds the peer's whole address is locked out: its browsers, control pages and PIN use on that machine. The design's 'degrade safely' section covers only new peers against an old Stagewatch. Its risk note ('all three peers implement the 60 s hold') is false for every deployed peer.
issues.evidence: AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:322-324 (onopen: delay=500), :333 (onclose -> _retry); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:183-186,200 (attempt=0 after a normal return); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:229-251 (attempt=0, Jitter.Shared.Redial(0)); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1077-1082 (unknown key counted), :1154-1163 (every header key goes through Authorize); today a refused key with no viewing code stays open with the public frame (:1164,1213-1219), so one failure per connection
issues.fix: Close on refusal or revocation only on sockets that opted into node links (node= present), since those peers honour retry. Legacy sockets get the verdict message and keep today's public-frame behaviour. Alternatively, land the peer units first (they degrade safely) and gate the close behind node=. Add a suite or e2e test: a legacy-style client (no node=, revoked key, 0.5 s redial) must not lock its address out within 60 s.

issues.issue: A binding conflict now cuts the timer. Operators commonly paste one node key into several installs: Patterns desk plus twin or standby, two AGMessages, or one 'show apps' key in all three peers. Today every holder follows the frames, and only the approval queue is first-come. Under the design, an upgraded second holder (node=Y with a key bound to X) is refused and closed, and loses the countdown, the app's core function, over a rule that governs contexts and approvals. Legacy holders (no node=) are admitted as node X because the id comes from the key's binding. So AGMessage and PlayMap sharing Patterns' key would all be listed, and grouped in ListNodes, as Patterns' node: a misidentification on the Show network and in the context peers.
issues.evidence: Design 2.1 refusal 'this key speaks for another node' then close 1008, and decision 2 (node key without node= is a node with the key's bound id); today BindKey is consulted only by proposals, collect and result (Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/Approvals.cs:92,137,154), and /ws ignores it (WebServer.cs:1154-1219); REMOTE.md 2.15 says only 'a node key is bound to the node it first spoke for; one app's key can't collect another's'
issues.fix: On /ws, answer a binding conflict with ok:true, verified:'none' and the conflict words (frames continue, no node privileges). Refuse only the node routes (context, proposals, collect, result) with 403. For legacy keyed sockets, do not assert the binding's id as their identity: list them as 'key <name>, id unproven'. Add the shared-key case to the risks and the release notes, with a journal row naming the key and both ids.

issues.issue: An unproven node= claim escapes the operator's Screens. Any page or script on the LAN can open /ws?node=x&t=y (no header is needed; browsers can set query strings). The socket then leaves Screens, is skipped by Push, Disconnect and Identify, and no node disconnect verb exists. 'Revoke its key' does not apply because there is no key. Today 'screen disconnect' can drop any such stray client.
issues.evidence: Design decision 7 and 4 ('screen … all never includes a node'; ListScreens filters Node is null; 'No node disconnect verb is added'); WebServer.cs:89-131 (Disconnect is today's tool for a stray tablet, per its doc comment)
issues.fix: Make only key-verified node links (a node key bound to that id) nodes. A node= claim without a node key stays a screen, flagged 'claims to be patterns 9f8e…', and keeps disconnect. Alternatively, add a one-off 'Drop this link' action on unverified Show network rows.

issues.issue: Node rows are unbounded and open to poisoning. 'A node with an open link but no hello is listed' in Show network and in the context's peers. On an open Stagewatch, one client can open hundreds of keyless node links with random ids. That grows the §6 peers array, which AGMessage's AI, Patterns' Eye and MCP get_context read, and the desk rows, without bound. This violates Stagewatch's 'bounded everything' doctrine, and PeerContexts itself caps at 32.
issues.evidence: Design 2.3 ('A node with an open link but no hello is listed'); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Core/ShowBus.cs:43 (MaxPeers = 32); Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md standing brief ('bounded everything')
issues.fix: Cap ListNodes and the context peers rows, and leave unverified link-only nodes out of the context entirely. Show them only on the desk, collapsed, as 'N unproven links'.

issues.issue: Release reopens a first-come race that the intended new holder always loses. Release drops the old holder's sockets with retry 1 (and old peers redial in about 0.5 s anyway), while the reinstalled peer that was refused sits in its 60 s hold. The old holder rebinds first. The design also contradicts itself: peers hold max(60, retry), so 'retry 1 — dial again' becomes 60 s for every patched peer.
issues.evidence: Design 2.1 ('the operator let this key speak for another node — dial again', retry 1) vs decision 'Peers redial no sooner than max(60, retry)'; AGMessage nodes.js:322-324 and Patterns StagewatchLinkService.cs:183-186 (legacy fast redial)
issues.fix: Make release an explicit rebind: from the Show network row or the key row, 'Let this key speak for <chosen node>', which writes the new pair at once. Define the peer hold as max(60, retry), except for an explicit 'released' code, or drop the retry-1 path.

issues.issue: KeysChanged would drop live links spuriously. A legacy node-key socket is admitted with no id ('none yet'). Its own first context POST then binds the key. Bound is persisted, the key list changes, RefreshScreenCopies calls KeysChanged, and the socket's recorded node (null) no longer equals NodeOf(key). The design gives no comparison rule, so the obvious one drops the link with the false words 'the operator let this key speak for another node'.
issues.evidence: Design SW-3/SW-4: 'RefreshScreenCopies copies Node and calls _web?.KeysChanged() when the key list changed'; 'KeysChanged() drops sockets whose key is gone or whose binding was released'
issues.fix: Drop on release only through an explicit release generation or event that names the key, never on a NodeOf mismatch. A socket with a null node whose key becomes bound adopts the id. Add a test: a legacy keyed socket stays open across its own first bind.

issues.issue: PlayMap's honest 'paired' introduces a regression and leaves a chain unfollowed. 'paired = Pairing == Paired' makes keyless links (scope none, NotNeeded) and links to an older Stagewatch with no key (Unknown) report paired:false. Preflight then turns such a link amber, 'heard but not paired', where today it is green. PlayMap's own Patterns link counts NotNeeded as paired. PlayMap's context item for the Stagewatch link never reads pairing or refusal. After a refusal and close, preflight says red 'is not heard (down)' with the fix 'LINK STAGEWATCH host', which is the wrong remedy for a refused key.
issues.evidence: Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/PatternsLink.cs:142 (Paired = Paired or NotNeeded); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Show/PreflightBreadth.cs:123-127; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/ContextBuilder.cs:96-100; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Host/NetworkHost.cs:309-316
issues.fix: Set paired = Pairing is Paired or NotNeeded. Carry Refused into LinkView, so that preflight says 'key refused — make or release a node key on Stagewatch' and the context item turns amber or red with those words. Name PreflightBreadth.cs and ContextBuilder.cs in the Mapper unit and check their round-3 ownership.

issues.issue: The peers' existing 403 words become false. Patterns maps any 403 on its context POST to 'the Stagewatch key may read but not post — make a node key' and any 403 on proposals to 'may not send proposals — a node key is needed'. PlayMap maps 401/403 to 'make a node key'. Both peers ignore a refused collect silently. With the design's new 403 'this key speaks for another node (<id>)' or 'node <id> speaks with its own key', every peer tells the operator the wrong remedy, and approved proposals quietly become 'undelivered'.
issues.evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:405-409,431-433,454-456; Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:510-513,528-531
issues.fix: In PT-1 and PM-1, read the error field of the 403 body and show it. Surface a refused collect in the link's words or STATE, and in Patterns' approval words.

issues.issue: The refusal hold can be lost to the close race. Stagewatch sends the verdict and then CloseOutputAsync, and disposes the stream. In PlayMap, Take returns the hold and ReceiveAsync then calls ws.CloseOutputAsync. If the peer has already torn the connection down, that call throws. RunAsync's catch then sets attempt++ with hold=Zero and redials on Jitter.Shared.Redial, a fast-redial path even for a patched peer. Patterns' RunAsync has the same shape.
issues.evidence: Mapper/src/PlayMap.Net/Links/StagewatchLink.cs:229-251 (hold only from a normal return), :361-366 (CloseOutputAsync after Take); Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:1182-1189 (send, CloseOutputAsync, return)
issues.fix: Record the refusal (Pairing=Refused, refusedUntil) in a field inside Take, before any I/O, and have RunAsync honour that field on every exit path. Test it with a FakeStagewatch that closes immediately after the verdict.

issues.issue: The Patterns test 'no redial before 60 s on the injected show clock' cannot be written as claimed. ShowClock is a static Stopwatch, not an injectable clock, and the redial waits on Task.Delay in real time.
issues.evidence: Patterns/src/Patterns.Core/Services/ShowClock.cs:12-23; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:200,204-208
issues.fix: Add a delay seam to StagewatchLinkService (a Func<TimeSpan,CancellationToken,Task> or a TimeProvider) and assert the requested hold. Alternatively, assert 'exactly one dial within N s' as the AGMessage and PlayMap tests do.

issues.issue: A peer-chosen name can shadow screen targets. The design refuses a screen command whose target is a node's id or name. A node's name comes from its own hello or context, so the peer controls it. A peer named 'Lobby TV', or 'all', could make the operator's 'screen identify Lobby TV' or 'screen identify all' refused, depending on the order of the checks. Screens.Match falls back to a name match.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/Screens.cs:61-68; design 2.4 ('A node's id or name as the target is refused')
issues.fix: Specify the order: 'all' or empty, then browser id, then browser name. Refuse as a show app only when no browser matches, and only by node id, or by a name from a key-verified node.

issues.issue: The design rejects 'refuse the upgrade with a 401' on a wrong claim. Since .NET 7, ClientWebSocketOptions.CollectHttpResponseDetails exposes HttpStatusCode and HttpResponseHeaders (Retry-After) on a failed ConnectAsync, and Node's ws raises 'unexpected-response'. A failed upgrade also makes legacy clients back off (onopen never fires; attempt++), where an upgrade followed by a close resets their backoff.
issues.evidence: Design decision 1 and 5 alternatives ('a .NET ClientWebSocket gets only an exception string'); AGMessage/app/lib/nodes.js:322-324,333; Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/StagewatchLinkService.cs:183-200
issues.fix: Re-weigh the alternatives: a 401 or 403 with Retry-After at upgrade for legacy keyed sockets is safer than upgrade then close. Keep the in-band verdict for node= links if words are wanted.

issues.issue: Over-building against the gaps' value. G06 is high, but G15 is medium and G32 and G43 are low. G43's own fix is AGMessage-only (an authenticated 2xx, which fetchContext already makes). The design adds a new in-band verdict protocol, retry semantics, persisted bindings, a release UI, a ScreenDirector extraction, rig options and changes in three peers: 12 units across 4 repos. That breadth is what creates the rollout hazard above.

Patterns' ShowBusIdentity falls back to a fresh id per run when patterns.node-id cannot be written (ShowBusNetwork.cs:186-189). With persisted bindings, that desk is refused after every restart. The design should say so, and Patterns should surface the unwritable id.
Coordination with the spec-1-3 design's 'Authorization: Window <token>': the node link's header parsing must not read a Window scheme as a key or PIN.
The order of the screen verb's matching: 'all', then browser id, then browser name, before any node refusal; and no node refusal by a peer-chosen name alone.
